description:
san_entry_matches_mailbox at pkix-identity/src/lib.rs:487-492 calls decode_utf8_string_any on the OtherName.value. If decode fails (e.g., the OtherName carries a BMPString or a malformed Utf8StringRef), the function returns false — the entry is silently skipped.

The verify_mailbox doc (lib.rs:469) lists MalformedSan as 'the SAN extension is present but cannot be parsed'. Currently MalformedSan is only returned when the outer SubjectAltName SEQUENCE itself fails to decode (find_san line 798). Inner per-entry malformation of an OtherName is treated as 'just doesn't match'.

The current behavior is defensible (liberal-in-what-you-accept, don't reject a whole match because one OtherName is corrupt). But it's not documented. A contributor reading the code will read decode_utf8_string_any returning Result<_, IdentityError::MalformedSan>, see it discarded as 'Err(_) => false', and wonder if that was intentional.

Suggested rewrite: add a one-line code comment on line 490 saying 'malformed OtherName values are skipped, not propagated — matching continues across remaining SAN entries' and add a corresponding sentence to the verify_mailbox rustdoc's MalformedSan entry: 'MalformedSan is returned only when the outer SubjectAltName SEQUENCE cannot be decoded; corruption inside an individual OtherName value is treated as non-match.'
title: Malformed otherName(SmtpUTF8Mailbox) value silently no-matches rather than propagating MalformedSan
